rationale: Feminine ordinal 'the third' with doubled article ⲧⲧ-. Already attested in glossary as ⲧⲙⲁⲍⲱⲁⲙⲧ. Used here to enumerate the third saying or third item in a teaching-series.

Verbal/predicate form on the same root as ⲡⲙⲁⲍⲁⲓ̈ⲡⲧⲉ 'hidden chamber.' Likely ⲙⲁ- ('place of') + ⲍⲁⲓⲡⲉ (variant of ⲍⲏⲡ qualitative of ϩⲱⲡ 'hide'). Functions verbally with subject prefix ϥ̄- 'he is hidden.' Distinct from but related to ⲍⲏⲡ 'hidden' attested elsewhere on this page.
Lyc. ⲭⲱⲣⲙⲉ = Sah. ϫⲱⲣⲙ 'make a sign, wink, signal.' Used here in the idiom ⲛⲟⲩⲭⲉ ⲛⲟⲩⲭⲱⲣⲙⲉ 'cast a sign' for the Savior's hidden communication to disciples about hidden mysteries.
Greek loanword διακρίνειν 'distinguish, discriminate.' Lycopolitan ⲁⲓⲁⲕⲣⲓⲛⲉ shows ⲇ→ⲁⲓ shift. Used here of failing to distinguish light-mystery from darkness-mystery.
Lycopolitan singular ⲡⲍⲟ (line 30) and plural ⲡⲍⲟⲟⲩⲉ for ϩⲟⲟⲩ 'day.' The phrase ⲛ̄ϣⲏⲣⲉ ⲙ̄ⲡⲍⲟⲟⲩⲉ 'sons of the day' echoes 1 Thess 5:5.
ⲡⲁ- (relational 'the one of') + ⲡⲍⲟⲟⲩⲉ ('the days'). 'The mystery of the day' as paired with 'the mystery of the night' (ⲡⲙⲩⲥⲧⲏⲣⲓⲟⲛ ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲩⲱⲏ).
